description: Synthetic continuum (N=5000, P=6, seed=7): does a single continuous predictor match/beat k=4 cluster-label dummies for outcome prediction? Reproduces Dennis et al. 2019 (PMID 31047901) logic in silico. Not real diabetes data.
method: Single 6D correlated Gaussian continuum; outcome = smooth function of underlying axes (linear + logistic); 5-fold CV; LinearRegression (R2) and LogisticRegression (AUC).
conclusion: Under a continuum, discretizing into 4 clusters underperforms even a single continuous feature, because clustering discards within-cluster gradient information. Mirrors the empirical Dennis finding that age-at-diagnosis alone matched clusters and eGFR beat clusters.
limitation: Synthetic; bears on evidence logic (continuum-vs-discretization), not on diabetes biology directly.
